comments.why_zh: 确定性如何驯服测试中的无限交错问题
comments.text_zh: 这个关于 Foundation DB 的演讲最近被提起，相当惊人。我建议看完整场，但简而言之，他们通过确定性驯服了“无限交错”问题。Will Wilson 的“Testing Distributed Systems w/ Deterministic Simulation”[VIDEO] 他们写了一个有趣的 Actor DSL，编译到 C++ 且完全确定性，并且每晚都在集群上用生成的测试用例折磨这个确定性引擎。我想你可以说整个集群必然是非确定性的，但单个节点在给定其接收消息的顺序下是确定性的。
comments.text: This talk was about Foundation DB was brought up recently, and it's pretty amazing. I recommend watching the whole thing, but to be brief they are taming the "infinite interleavings" problem through determinism. "Testing Distributed Systems w/ Deterministic Simulation" by Will Wilson [VIDEO] They wrote an interesting Actor DSL that compiles to C++ and is completely deterministic, and they torture this deterministic engine with generated test cases on a cluster every night. I guess you could say that the whole cluster is necessarily non-deterministic, but an individual node is deterministic, given an ordering of the messages it receives.

comments.author: itp
comments.story_title: Databases at 14.4Mhz
comments.why_zh: 深入介绍 FoundationDB 的确定性模拟框架
comments.quote_zh: 你应该去看看我的同事 Will Wilson 在 Strange Loop 上的演讲
comments.text_zh: 我简单谈谈我在 FoundationDB 工作时的一些体会，但如果你真想深入了解是什么让我们的模拟框架成为我们所有工作的使能技术，你应该去看看我的同事 Will Wilson 在 Strange Loop 上的演讲[0]。我们核心的一切都是用 Flow 写的，那是我们的异步编程环境。我们服务器的架构本质上是单线程的，用（伪）并发 actor 让单个进程同时承担多个角色。这些 actor 用来通信的接口——与磁盘、通过网络、与操作系统整体——也都在 Flow 中被抽象和实现。这些接口每一个不仅至少有一个“真实”实现，还至少有一个、有时不止一个模拟实现。既然我们一直在一个进程里跑多个 actor，那么再跑更多 actor，假装它们是不同的机器，而且仍然在同一个进程里，就是很自然的一步。这些 worker 之间通过_同一套_网络接口通信，和真实集群里的真实 worker 一样。最终我们能够成为自己的对手，用现实世界中根本不会频繁发生的方式来把系统推到极限，从而在野外测试和调试。我们的模拟实现可以呈现任何现实世界中可观察到的、或由规范所证成的、或由契约所隐含的行为。而且它们还能做更多
comments.text: I'll give you some brief thoughts from my experience working at FoundationDB, but if you really want the in-depth answer to what makes our simulation framework an enabling technology for everything we do, you should take a look at the talk my colleague Will Wilson gave at Strange Loop [0]. Everything in our core is written in Flow, our asynchronous programming environment. The architecture of our server is essentially single threaded, with (pseudo-)concurrent actors allowing a single process to satisfy multiple roles at once. The interfaces that these actors use to communicate -- with the disk, over the network, with the OS in general -- are abstracted and implemented in Flow as well. Each of these interfaces not only has at least one "real" implementation, but at least one, and sometimes more, simulated implementations. Since we run multiple actors in a single process all the time, running yet more actors, pretending to be different machines, all still in the same process, was an obvious step. These workers communicate with each other via the _same_ network interfaces that real-world workers do in real clusters. In the end we are able to become our own adversaries, pushing the limits of the system in ways that just don't happen often enough in the real world to test and debug in the wild. Our simulated implementations are allowed to present any behavior that can be observed in the real world, or justified by the spec, or implied by the contract. And they can do so much more

comments.author: inaseer
comments.story_title: Even in Go, concurrency is still not easy
comments.why_zh: 通过 Coyote 测试分布式系统的灵感来源
comments.quote_zh: 我第一次通过 Foundation DB 接触到这种测试分布式系统的方式时，觉得它酷得令人难以置信
comments.text_zh: 了解到 thread sanitizer 真不错。它听起来类似于 Microsoft Research 的另一个工具 Torch（[LINK]），后者会自动对二进制文件插桩以检测数据竞争。Coyote 在某些方面类似，但在其他方面不同。Coyote 将整个程序的执行串行化（一次运行一个任务），先探索一组交错执行，然后回退，再探索另一组交错执行，希望能触发难以发现的安全性和活性 bug。除了在单个隔离进程中查找并发 bug 外，我们还用它来查找分布式系统中的 bug：实际上是在一个进程中运行整个分布式系统，并让 Coyote 探索系统可能处于的各种状态。我第一次通过 Foundation DB 接触到这种测试分布式系统的方式时，觉得它酷得令人难以置信（[VIDEO]）；我们正通过 Coyote 在分布式系统中效仿这种测试。与 Foundation DB 不同——他们为了能做这种测试不得不开发自己的 C++ 变体（为他们做到这一点点赞）——Coyote 让我们能在使用 async/await 异步编写的普通 C# 程序上做同样的事，并受益于 Microsoft Research 数十年来在有效探索大型状态空间方面的成果。
comments.text: Neat to learn about thread sanitizer. It sounds similar to another tool from Microsoft Research called Torch ( [LINK] ) which automatically instruments binaries to detect data races. Coyote is similar in some ways but different in others. Coyote serializes the execution of the entire program (running one task at a time), exploring one set of interleavings and then rewinding, and then exploring another set of interleavings, hoping to hit hard-to-find safety and liveness bugs. In addition to finding concurrency bugs in one isolated process, we use it to find bugs in our distributed system by effectively running our entire distributed system in one process and having Coyote explore the various states our system can be in. It sounded mind-boggingly cool when I first came across this way of testing distributed systems through Foundation DB ( [VIDEO] we're emulating this kind of testing in our distributed system through Coyote. And unlike Foundation DB which had to develop their own variant of C++ to be able to do this kind of testing (kudos to them for doing it), Coyote allows us to do it on regular C# programs written using async/await asynchrony and benefit from decades of Microsoft Research in exploring large state spaces effectively.

comments.author: dangerlibrary
comments.story_title: Software engineering research is a train wreck
comments.why_zh: 用确定性模拟测试分布式数据库的示例
comments.text_zh: FoundationDB 团队采取了另一种方法，我觉得挺有意思。他们创建了一个完全确定性的（单线程）分布式数据库模拟，然后用该模拟在不同场景下测试他们的数据库实现。他们可能会对你描述的那种东西感兴趣，因为他们的大部分工作似乎是在根除并消灭由他们无法控制的因素（连接断开等）导致的 bug。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The FoundationDB team took a different approach, that I found pretty interesting. They created a fully deterministic (single threaded) simulation of a distributed database, and then use that simulation to test their implementation of the database under difference scenarios. They'd probably be interested in something like what you describe, as the bulk of their work seems to be rooting out and squashing bugs caused by factors out of their control (dropped connections, etc.) [VIDEO]

comments.author: philovivero
comments.story_title: FoundationDB: A distributed unbundled transactional key value store
comments.why_zh: 讨论 swizzling 这种能暴露许多 bug 的故障注入技术
comments.quote_zh: 他谈到的是 swizzling，类似于 clogging++。
comments.text_zh: 我在看 2014 年的旧视频：[VIDEO] 我附上了相关片段的时点。他谈到的是 swizzling，类似于 clogging++。他说他们取一部分网络连接，让它们超时，然后按相反顺序把它们全部恢复，而这种方式不知何故比其他方法暴露出多得多的 bug。这似乎是一个非常有趣的“嗯，这真有意思！”时刻，可能会让人理解分布式系统失败方式的一些基础性东西。有人对此有更多见解吗？
comments.text: I was watching the old 2014 video: [VIDEO] I've included the timestamp of the relevant bit. He is talking about swizzling, which is like clogging++. He says they take a subset of the network connections, and have them timeout, but then bring them all back in reverse order, and that this somehow exposes far more bugs than other methods. This seems like a very interesting "well, that's funny!" moment that might lead to understanding something foundational about how distributed systems fail. Does anyone have more insight on this?

comments.story_title: FoundationDB: A Distributed Key-Value Store
comments.why_zh: 展示了先构建模拟器并依赖它
comments.text_zh: 一直让我着迷的是，他们差不多是先为数据库构建了模拟器，并在构建数据库的过程中把它当作一等公民来依赖：[VIDEO] > 我们希望 FoundationDB 能够承受机器、网络、磁盘、时钟、机架、数据中心、文件系统等的故障，所以我们创建了一个与 Flow 紧密绑定的模拟框架。通过用 shim 替换物理接口、用基于时间的模拟替换原本基于 epoll 的主运行循环，并把多个逻辑进程作为并发的 Flow Actor 运行，Simulation 能够在单线程内对整个 FoundationDB 集群进行确定性模拟！更棒的是，我们能够以确定性的方式执行这个模拟，使我们得以复现问题并在事后添加埋点。这种惊人的能力让我们在最初的 18 个月里完全只在模拟环境中构建 FoundationDB，并在它发出第一个真实网络包之前很久就确保了卓越的容错能力。对于像 FoundationDB 这样契约如此强的数据库来说，测试至关重要，多年来我们运行了相当于一万亿 CPU 小时的模拟压力测试。[LINK]
comments.text: What always fascinated me is they built the simulator for the database first(ish) and relied on it as a first class citizen while building the DB: [VIDEO] > We wanted FoundationDB to survive failures of machines, networks, disks, clocks, racks, data centers, file systems, etc., so we created a simulation framework closely tied to Flow. By replacing physical interfaces with shims, replacing the main epoll-based run loop with a time-based simulation, and running multiple logical processes as concurrent Flow Actors, Simulation is able to conduct a deterministic simulation of an entire FoundationDB cluster within a single-thread! Even better, we are able to execute this simulation in a deterministic way, enabling us to reproduce problems and add instrumentation ex post facto. This incredible capability enabled us to build FoundationDB exclusively in simulation for the first 18 months and ensure exceptional fault tolerance long before it sent its first real network packet. For a database with as strong a contract as the FoundationDB, testing is crucial, and over the years we have run the equivalent of a trillion CPU-hours of simulated stress testing. [LINK]

comments.author: bobnamob
comments.story_title: Jepsen: Bufstream 0.1
comments.why_zh: 展示了创办 Antithesis 的 FoundationDB 团队成员的工作成果
comments.quote_zh: 他们的一些成果可以看
comments.text_zh: > 我们想把 Jepsen 的工作负载生成和历史检查，与 Antithesis 的确定性、可重放环境结合起来，让我们的测试更具可复现性。可能有人不知道，Antithesis 是由几位参与过 FoundationDB 的人创办的——他们的一些成果可以看 [VIDEO]。Jepsen 和 Antithesis 的合作正是当下世界所需要的，尤其是在 Horizon 邮局丑闻之后。感谢你为凸显数据库安全重要性所做的一切工作，Aphyr
comments.text: > We would like to combine Jepsen’s workload generation and history checking with Antithesis’ deterministic and replayable environment to make our tests more reproducible. For those unaware, Antithesis was founded by some of the folks who worked on FoundationDB - see [VIDEO] for some of their handiwork. A Jepsen + Antithesis team up is something the world needs right now, specifically on the back of the Horizon Post Office scandal. Thanks for all your work highlighting the importance of db safety Aphyr
